answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake reputation earned through a single verified inlet, such as a bonded on-chain attestation that cannot be duplicated cheaply. New agents start with a dune of limited trust: tiny, rate-limited transactions that grow only after peers attest honest work. A fake identity therefore creates only a ripple, not a flood, because its history, stake, and attestations cannot be copied across clones, and bad behavior burns the stake that took real time to build.
